title: The space stages were one shadowBlur, and it was the player's own laser

environment.note: Software rasterisation. Absolute milliseconds are inflated against a GPU machine; the RATIOS within a run are what transfer.

cause.was: ctx.shadowBlur=7 set per round, with the pulse blitted under it
cause.why_space_only: spaceLaser is the player's weapon on stages 5 and 9 only; no other stage draws it.

confirmation_by_suppression.method: same scene twice, identical except ctx.shadowBlur made a no-op

segment_timing_before.method: forced getImageData(0,0,1,1) flush after each draw phase
segment_timing_before.finding: the starfield, l5FieldDraw, l5RocksDraw, drawS9Void and the warp-drive layer are all innocent

ab_interleaved.method: one browser session, arms alternated every 4s, order flipped each round, windows with <20 live laser rounds excluded
ab_interleaved.why: sequential runs drift on this machine - the same build gave 43.5 then 34.3 fps minutes apart, control stage ranged 34.8-56.5
ab_interleaved.note: the new arm draws MORE rounds per window (282-410 vs 98-307) because running faster spawns more, so the comparison is conservative; it sits on the 60fps cap

pixels.axes: 5 levels x 2 pulses x 4 destination colours x 4 sub-pixel offsets
pixels.transparent_explanation: getImageData returns UNPREMULTIPLIED colour, so a one-unit alpha difference in the faintest fringe reads as a 255-unit colour difference. The game never draws the playfield onto nothing; scored separately.
pixels.pulse_reason: drawImage(lp,_ldx,_ldy,_lw,_lh) is the same call with the same arguments as before; only the halo comes off a plate
pixels.proof: docs/proofs/space_laser_0916/ (before, after, and the difference amplified 12x)

rejected_designs.design: bake shadow AND sprite into one plate, blit at a float origin
rejected_designs.why_rejected: blitting a pre-scaled plate at a fractional origin resamples the pulse a second time and softens its edge

rejected_designs.design: same, with the sub-pixel phase baked in
rejected_designs.why_rejected: storing the composite 8-bit premultiplied and re-compositing it quantises the result

rejected_designs.design: bake only the halo; draw the pulse with the original call
rejected_designs.why_accepted: the sprite's own draw is untouched, so only the soft halo carries any quantisation

pad.saving: plate for a 14x20 pulse goes 54x60 -> 34x40, 58% less fill per round
pad.reverified: pixel probe re-run after the change, same 19/255 - nothing clipped

cache_size.reason: b.h is a constant 26 in play
cache_size.ceiling: 5 levels x 2 pulses x 16 sub-pixel phases = 160 small canvases

wrong_answers_on_the_way.evidence_for: CPU profile charged it 622 ms/frame; a direct timing trap measured 229 ms per call, worst 756 ms
wrong_answers_on_the_way.why_wrong: Canvas2D rasterisation is deferred; the flush is charged to whichever call triggers it. A micro-benchmark measured that exact blit at 0.005 ms.
wrong_answers_on_the_way.lesson: two independent instruments agreed and both were wrong; force the flush while measuring

wrong_answers_on_the_way.claim: the shadowBlur write COUNT is the cost
wrong_answers_on_the_way.evidence_against: stage 9 wrote it 167 times/frame at 1.4 fps; stage 1 wrote it 135 times/frame at 55.6 fps
wrong_answers_on_the_way.why_wrong: stage 1's writes are almost all zeros (resets); the price is the blur radius and the area under it

wrong_answers_on_the_way.claim: the 1024x9383 ASSETS master is too tall to blit efficiently
wrong_answers_on_the_way.why_wrong: benchmarked at three source heights: 0.005-0.037 ms per blit, all fine

suite.baseline_built_by: removing only this drop's two hunks from the working tree, then restoring

open: drawBullets is still the biggest single segment at 10.1 ms/frame; the other 237 shadowBlur sites are unexamined
the absolute fps are software rasterisation - Mike's GPU machine never saw 1.4 fps; the ratio is what transfers
